transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Aurum Procurement), Sonia R. Diaz (Aurum Legal), Ethan Wu (Aurum Platform)

Auto-summary: 
- Short alignment on commercial gating: MSA + DPA must be agreed before procurement issues PO.
- Technical pilot for two weeks to validate latency and multi-tenant isolation.
- Action items captured; next call in one week or after MSA redline review.

Topics: MSA redline focus, DPA addendum, SLA tier options, technical pilot details, KMS keying options, SSO, pricing tiers, procurement timeline.

00:00 Jordan Ellis: "Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick intros then we'll jump into the MSA redlines and the SLA ask from your procurement team. Jordan from Redwood, Maya our SE..."
00:22 Liam O'Connor: "Hi, Liam here. We're mainly trying to get timeline, the DPA language, and cost buckets clear for exec review. We typically need legal OK before Finance signs off."
00:35 Sonia R. Diaz: "Sonia, counsel. We'll be looking at data residency, subcontractor list and right to audit. Also curious about key management — do you support customer-controlled KMS?"
00:50 Maya Patel: "Yes, we do support KMS integrations, we have both cloud KMS and an option for customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private modes. On hosted we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own key via our KMS connector, though there's some caveats re: egress logging."
01:10 Ethan Wu: "By caveats you mean egress fees or log retention? We need to know if logs will contain PII before we proceed."
01:22 Maya Patel: "Right; logs can be configured. For Private deployments we can turn off token-level logging and only keep service metrics. For hosted there's anonymization but we can provide SOC2 attestation and per-request metadata in audit logs if needed."
02:05 Jordan Ellis: "From the procurement perspective, we usually provide a standard MSA + a DPA addendum. What would help us is specific redlines from Aurum legal — are there must-haves?"
02:18 Sonia R. Diaz: "Mainly: data residency in EU for European customers, subprocessor list, 30 day notice for any subprocessor changes — and the usual indemnity caps. Also, standard SLA credits model — we need clarity on calculation of downtime and crediting mechanism."
02:45 Jordan Ellis: "Understood. We have SLA tiers: Bronze/Silver/Gold — availability percentages and latency SLOs differ. We can move Gold to a dedicated pool with stronger guarantees. I'll put the exact percentages in the redline."
03:10 Liam O'Connor: "Procurement will need a rate-card too; how soon can we get committed pricing for a pilot vs production? We have an internal thresholds for escalation if expected TCO exceeds our model."
03:32 Jordan Ellis: "We can give a pilot rate and a committed reserved capacity quote, usually pilot hourly or free credits for two weeks. Production reserved pricing requires a 12-month commit for dedicated capacity — we can put options in the SOW."
04:05 Maya Patel: "Technical note on pilot: we'll use a staging VPC peered to your environment, run a continuous batching workload to simulate your 512-token average request size. We'll instrument KV cache hit rates and tail latency (95/99 pctl)."
04:30 Ethan Wu: "Sounds good. For the pilot we want 95th <= 200ms for short chats, and under 400ms for longer flows. Is that realistic?"
04:45 Maya Patel: "For hosted, depending on model, 95th under 200ms is ambitious but achievable on optimized LLMs with proper batching and cache. For dedicated we can hit that reliably. There are tradeoffs: quantization can reduce latency but may slightly affect quality."
05:12 Sonia R. Diaz: "Also we need to understand data purging timelines. If we request data deletion, what's the window for removing logs and cached prefixes?"
05:26 Maya Patel: "We have data retention config: immediate deletion of customer data in Private; in hosted we have up to 30 days retention by default but can agree to shorter retention in the DPA. KV cache purging is immediate on request, but cached data in multi-tenant layers is handled via TTLs and strict scoping."
06:00 Jordan Ellis: "Okay commercial path: Jordan to send MSA redline focused on DPA & SLA, Maya to provide benchmark plan, Aurum to give expected QPS and list of compliance needs (KMS, SSO). After MSA agreed we'll do pilot then Finance will route PO."
06:28 Liam O'Connor: "FYI our standard procurement cadence: legal signoff -> finance review (3-5 business days) -> PO issuance. If legal hits major exceptions that might stretch it out. We aim to close by end of month if all goes well."
07:05 (background chatter) Speaker 2: "uh-huh"
07:22 Jordan Ellis: "On SLA credits — the contract calculates credits as a percent of monthly fee based on downtime windows. We can walk through sample calculations in the SOW. Also, we can provide weekly reporting if you need continuous visibility."
07:50 Sonia R. Diaz: "We prefer a measurable SLA tied to specific endpoints and a defined on-call escalation matrix. Also want the right to audit subprocessors and a copy of SOC2 reports."
08:12 Maya Patel: "We can provide SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation packages. For audits, we provide third-party reports; direct audits of Redwood infrastructure are done under special circumstances and usually limited to Dedicated/Private customers with an executed NDA and scoping."
09:00 Ethan Wu: "If we go Dedicated can we also get a runbook for incident response and a technical contact list? That's needed for our SRE team."
09:18 Maya Patel: "Yes, runbook and a named SE for the pilot and initial onboarding window. We'll also add tracing hooks and a per-route cost breakdown in the console so you can see token cost by call."
10:05 Liam O'Connor: "About pricing approvals — does Redwood have a standard escalation for discounts if we commit to 18 months?"
10:20 Jordan Ellis: "We have standard tiered discounts for longer commitments. For >12 months we can propose a custom reserved capacity rate. I'll include a few example scenarios: 6-mo evaluation, 12-mo standard commit, 18-mo/24-mo custom pricing. Discounts scale with committed QPS and reserved GPUs."
11:00 Sonia R. Diaz: "We also need indemnity language and limitation of liability aligned with our procurement policy (capped at X months revenue) — expect redlines there."
11:20 Jordan Ellis: "Noted. We'll flag those as likely negotiation points. For fastest path, it helps if you provide the procurement playbook or standard MSA template we should align to."
11:40 Liam O'Connor: "I'll upload a short procurement checklist after this call. It includes approvers and maximum allowed indemnity caps per our policy."
12:05 Jordan Ellis: "Perfect. Quick technical deep-dive: Maya, can you outline the pilot topology?"
12:12 Maya Patel: "Topology: staging VPC peered to Aurum, a dedicated worker pool (if requested) for isolating pilot, sample load generator, point-in-time KV cache snapshots, and a metrics dashboard. We'll run 2-week tests simulating peak hour traffic for three sample flows."
13:00 Ethan Wu: "Do you support bring-your-own model weights /on-prem hosting for sensitive data?"
13:12 Maya Patel: "Private deployment supports customer-managed models; we ship a package that can be air-gapped. That's part of Redwood Private offering, usually under enterprise licensing. That adds ops overhead but gives full control."
13:45 Sonia R. Diaz: "If we require on-prem, we'd need clearer SLAs and runbooks; plus support windows need to be agreed."
14:00 Jordan Ellis: "We'll note that as an option but it'll move to enterprise track. For now pilot aims to validate hosted/Dedicated depending on your preference."
14:30 Liam O'Connor: "One more point on DPA: data subject rights and deletion flow — we need a demonstrable process for deletion, and for any backups how long data persists."
14:58 Maya Patel: "We log deletion events and have runbooks to scrub caches; backup retention policies can be set in the DPA. We'll propose a 30-day maximum for backups unless you need stricter terms."
15:30 Jordan Ellis: "Any competitor concerns?"
15:40 Liam O'Connor: "We're also evaluating Anthropic and BigCloud AI for pricing and regional footprint — but Redwood's overt emphasis on production-grade inference and clear pilot plan is attractive."
16:05 Maya Patel: "Good to hear. On performance specs we'll show comparative numbers but won't name specific competitor internal metrics."
16:30 (short pause)
16:45 Jordan Ellis: "Let's close with immediate next steps: I'll send the MSA redline by EOD Friday, Maya will share the benchmark plan and test harness, and Aurum will provide QPS/latency targets plus procurement playbook. Any objections?"
17:10 Sonia R. Diaz: "No objections, but will review the MSA quickly and mark non-starters. Please flag any third-party subprocessors in the first pass."
17:30 Liam O'Connor: "Procurement will expect the PO template; if legal approves we'll try to move fast."
17:50 Jordan Ellis: "Great. We'll schedule a follow-up in one week to go over MSA redlines and bench plan results. If legal issues are significant we'll extend timeline accordingly."
18:05 Ethan Wu: "We'll also try to give a list of three production flows and the expected token sizes to help Maya size the pilot."
18:20 Jordan Ellis: "Perfect — thanks everyone. End of call."

Questions: 
- Sonia: Is there any automatic subprocessor notification window? (Answer: 30 days for hosted; can be contractually extended)
- Ethan: Can Redwood provide a sample runbook for incident response? (Answer: yes — SE will provide)
